hints: The spring has zero applied force at a length of 20 cm, so calculate extension from that natural length.
Use a clear graph point such as 30 N at 60 cm, and convert the extension to metres before calculating k.
walkthrough: At zero force the spring length is 20 cm. At 30 N its length is 60 cm, so its extension is 40 cm = 0.40 m.
Using F = kx, k = F/x = 30/0.40 = 75 N m⁻¹.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses k = F/x, or the gradient of force against extension.
Uses a 0.40 m extension for 30 N to obtain k = 75 N m⁻¹.

hints: Read the spring length at 15 N and subtract the 20 cm natural length to find extension.
The stored energy is the triangular area under the force–extension graph, or use E = ½Fx.
walkthrough: At 15 N the graph gives a spring length of 40 cm, so the extension is 40 − 20 = 20 cm = 0.20 m.
The elastic potential energy is E = ½Fx = ½ × 15 × 0.20 = 1.5 J.
This is also the triangular area under the force–extension graph.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses the triangular graph area, ½Fx, ½kx², or an equivalent elastic-energy relationship.
Uses F = 15 N and x = 0.20 m, or k = 75 N m⁻¹ with x = 0.20 m.
Obtains elastic potential energy of 1.5 J.
